evidenceAudit.scope: Women with heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) in India: assessment, anaemia and endometrial pathology work-up, control of acute heavy bleeding, medical and surgical treatment, and referral. Built on the ICMR Heavy Menstrual Bleeding workflow (December 2025), with the mefenamic acid dose from its US label.
findings: History, examination, pictorial blood assessment chart, investigations, 12 mm endometrial thickness cut-off, age-40 sampling pathway, cancer risk factors, acute tranexamic acid regimen, transfusion threshold, norethisterone and medroxyprogesterone regimens, levonorgestrel intrauterine system (LNG-IUS), surgical options and referral checked against the ICMR HMB STW (December 2025).
Mefenamic acid dose taken from the US label (dysmenorrhoea dosing) because the ICMR STW gives none.
unverifiedSections: The ICMR STW does not define HMB or use the PALM-COEIN classification.
Combined oral contraceptive, iron and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) doses are not given in the STW and are not dosed here.
Gonadotrophin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogues are not mentioned in the STW.
Some flowchart branches of the STW are ambiguous; the age-40 and 12 mm pathways are summarised as read.
Drug cautions and contraindications without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.
US labels (DailyMed) were used where Indian sources give no dose; confirm against the Indian product label (CDSCO) and hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Heavy menstrual bleeding is a common cause of iron-deficiency anaemia in Indian women. Causes include fibroids, polyps, adenomyosis, endometrial hyperplasia or cancer, ovulatory dysfunction, thyroid disease, bleeding disorders and intrauterine devices. Assessment aims to exclude pregnancy, measure the anaemia, find structural or endometrial pathology (ultrasound endometrial thickness and sampling by age and risk) and treat medically before surgery, especially in younger women (ICMR STW). Acute heavy bleeding with haemoglobin below 7 g/dL needs transfusion and referral.
keyMechanisms: Structural lesions (fibroids, polyps, adenomyosis) enlarge the bleeding surface and impair contraction.
Anovulation leaves unopposed oestrogen, thickening the endometrium (hyperplasia risk).
Increased local fibrinolysis in the endometrium; tranexamic acid blocks it.
Bleeding disorders and anticoagulants impair haemostasis.

symptoms: Heavy or prolonged periods; clots; flooding
physicalSigns: Pallor — mild, moderate or severe (ICMR STW)
Tachycardia, low blood pressure in acute bleeding
Thyroid, liver or bleeding signs (ICMR STW)
redFlags: Haemoglobin below 7 g/dL or ongoing heavy blood loss: transfuse and refer (ICMR STW)
Atypical hyperplasia or malignancy on sampling (ICMR STW)
No relief or recurrence despite treatment (ICMR STW)
precipitants: Obesity, polycystic ovaries, diabetes, low parity (endometrial cancer risk) (ICMR STW)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Positive pregnancy test — exclude first (ICMR STW).
Mass or cavity lesion on ultrasound (ICMR STW).
Thick endometrium, age over 40 or risk factors; sampling (ICMR STW).
Abnormal bleeding or clotting time; family history (ICMR STW).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Haemoglobin below 7 g/dL or acute ongoing blood loss.
Ultrasound cut-off 12 mm; above 12 mm or high cancer risk (low parity, obesity, polycystic ovaries, diabetes) leads to sampling.
Thickened endometrium, hyperplasia or atypical hyperplasia; pathways split at age 40 and for postmenopausal women.
No relief after 3–6 months of medical treatment; conservative treatment first, especially in younger women.

clinicalManagement.title: Acute heavy bleeding
actions: IV tranexamic acid 1 g slowly, then oral tranexamic acid (ICMR STW).
Transfuse if haemoglobin below 7 g/dL; refer to a higher centre (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Assess
actions: Exclude pregnancy (with consent), then speculum and pelvic examination (ICMR STW).
Haemoglobin, smear, bleeding and clotting times, TSH, ultrasound (ICMR STW).
Endometrial sampling by thickness, age and risk (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Medical treatment
actions: Tranexamic acid during heavy days; add mefenamic acid if painful (ICMR STW).
Cyclical norethisterone or medroxyprogesterone from day 5 for 3 weeks, 4–6 cycles; or LNG-IUS (ICMR STW).
Combined oral contraceptives where contraception is wanted; haematinics; treat thyroid or bleeding disorders (ICMR STW).
Counselling is an important adjunct (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Surgical options
actions: Hysterectomy if no relief after 3–6 months of medical treatment (ICMR STW).
Refer atypical hyperplasia or malignancy (ICMR STW).

medicationPlan.note: Tranexamic acid, norethisterone, medroxyprogesterone and LNG-IUS from the ICMR HMB STW (December 2025); mefenamic acid dose from its US label. Norethisterone gives the best haemostasis among progestogens (ICMR STW). Iron, combined pill and NSAID doses are not given in the STW. Not clinically reviewed.

learningObjectives: Know when to sample the endometrium.
Use tranexamic acid and progestogens correctly.
keyPoints: Haemoglobin below 7 g/dL: transfuse and refer.
Endometrium 12 mm or more, age over 40 or risk factors: sample.
Medical treatment for 3–6 months before hysterectomy.
pitfalls: Missing endometrial cancer in an obese diabetic woman over 40.
Hysterectomy without trying medical treatment in young women.
Tranexamic acid with a thrombosis history.
